description: Near-black, slit all over, bright copper standing in every slit. Blows land harder and the armour that stops them fails.
lore: New hands rub the copper on a cloth, expecting the orange to come away. It never does — the first sign this is not rust in the ordinary sense — and it is warm, which rust is not. The trade grades on the copper regardless: bright, and running the full length of the slits, is a prime one; brown and pinched out is a dry one, and a dry one does noticeably less to the other man's armour.

The odd part is that no two carry the same rust. One kind of animal, one kind of stone — there is no argument about that part — but one comes up coppery, one near black, one with a green in it, and the difference is not the animal. What pressed down in here is iron that was never its own: somebody's left-out things going off in the weather, year over year, beside [[monsters/hedgehog|a small kept appointment]].

[[characters/7a779de1|Wendell]] was handed a green-tinged one at the fire a few winters back and turned it in the light a long time. The green, he said, was paint; he could name the gate it flaked off, and the wall the gate hung in. Then he talked until the fire was low, and for once — ask anyone who knows the old man — he named no price.
gm_notes: The paint-green stones and the Quillkin's garden are one place — this pairs with the hedgehog record's unpaid-evening hook. The gate's colour (green) is now canon; the garden-owner's name stays GM-coined, per that record.
